summary: Discovery + scoping call to align on POC objectives: validate OpenAI-compatible integration, run performance and cost benchmarks for Halcyon's retrieval-augmented generation workloads, and agree on timeline and artifacts for a 48-hour pilot. Customer will supply traces and prompt templates; Redwood will provide harness and initial config recommendations.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-24 15:30 UTC | Duration approx 55 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (AE), Sofia (SE) — Ethan (CTO), Lina (Sr ML Eng), Marco (Product)

[00:00] Jordan Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick intros? i'll kick off, i'm jordan, ag- account exec on the infra team. sofia is our se who will run the benchmarks with you.
[00:12] Ethan Brooks: thanks, jordan. ethan here, cto at halcyon. lina and marco are with me.
[00:16] Lina Zhao: hi all.
[00:18] Marco Silva: hey.
[00:21] Sofia Ruiz: great, quick agenda — align on success criteria, share workload sizing, talk bench plan and SDK integration paths, then timelines. sound good?
[00:28] Ethan Brooks: yes. we want to validate two things: 1) we can hit our latency SLOs with an openai-compatible flow and 2) quantify cost delta between hosted and dedicated. also security — we need VPC/KMS.
[00:40] Jordan Patel: perfect. can you remind us of current qps/tpm and typical prompt sizes?
[00:46] Lina Zhao: on avg it's 12 QPS during peak, spike to 35 for short bursts. tokens per request, pre-token about 200 to 600 depending on context, post-token generation averages 150 tokens. monthly active users about 120k, but pilot we'll simulate a 10k DAU slice.
[01:10] Marco Silva: main feature is an RAG flow, so there are embed calls and a generation step, critical to keep generation latency under 300ms p95 for the mobile client.
[01:22] Sofia Ruiz: okay that helps — so our bench should model a two-step pipeline: 1) embedding calls at lower latency sensitivity, 2) generation with context ~800 tokens. we need to capture KV warm/cold cache behavior since you keep session state often.
[01:37] Ethan Brooks: can you... sorry, clarify KV cache? we use a short-term conversation cache on our side — will that change results?
[01:44] Sofia Ruiz: yes, if the model runtime can reuse kv cache it reduces compute. we can test both cache-warm and cold scenarios.
[01:50] Jordan Patel: on integration surface: you said you prefer OpenAI-compatible endpoints. our platform supports an openai-style REST API and we have SDKs (js/py/go) with function-calling helpers and structured output validators. that should map to your clients with minimal changes.
[02:05] Lina Zhao: good. can you confirm function calling semantics? we rely on tool execution for DB lookups and a product taxonomy service.
[02:12] Sofia Ruiz: we support function/tool calling; it's compatible with the OpenAI function call spec, including name/params/required fields. small note — sometimes the param types are inferred slightly differently, transcription example — but we ship a schema validator to enforce structured JSON output.
[02:30] Marco Silva: so we'd define a JSON schema for the product API output and the model would be constrained?
[02:34] Sofia Ruiz: exactly. we can run a structured-output regression harness so we measure how often the model adheres to schema. this is part of quality success criteria.
[02:43] Ethan Brooks: good. on security, we need SOC2, audit logs, SSO, and KMS integration. also for production we want VPC peering or Private deployment — what's the delta on latency and setup time?
[02:56] Jordan Patel: short answer: our Private option gives you customer-managed VPC and the lowest egress risk. Dedicated (reserved) gives isolation and predictable throughput with shorter onboarding than full Private. latency differences are usually single-digit ms; networking setup may add a week for Dedicated and 3–4 weeks for Private depending on ops. we can provide a checklist.
[03:16] Lina Zhao: okay timeline wise, we're hoping to have a pilot within two weeks. is that realistic?
[03:21] Sofia Ruiz: two weeks for a shallow smoke? yes. for a full 48-hour benchmark with infra and data traces, i'd say schedule it week of march 9 as jordan suggested in pre-call notes. we need your traces and a test harness configured.
[03:33] Marco Silva: what will the bench measure?
[03:36] Sofia Ruiz: primary — p50/p95/p99 latency for generations, tokens/sec, throughput at target concurrency, error rates, and schema adherence rates for structured outputs. secondary — cost per 1k tokens for each profile, and degradation when we simulate node failures.
[03:51] Ethan Brooks: how do you simulate degradation?
[03:53] Sofia Ruiz: we can run controlled node drain and scale-down events and measure tail latency and fallback behavior. Redwood runtime supports automatic fallback to smaller model variants but that can affect quality; we will capture metrics and sample outputs for human eval.
[04:07] Lina Zhao: human eval — will you run quality checks? we need to see rouge/bleu or some semantic metrics plus product-specific correctness.
[04:15] Sofia Ruiz: yes we'll include automated checks (semantic similarity via embeddings) and sample a 500-response human review set. we can also plug your in-house eval scripts if you share them.
[04:25] Jordan Patel: back to integration — SDKs: we recommend using our JS SDK for the mobile backend and Python for any server-side orchestration. the SDKs wrap function calling and streaming. you can also talk direct to the openai-compatible endpoints if you prefer.
[04:39] Marco Silva: straight http calls would be easiest for our infra team, but we like the validators SDK offers. is the SDK open-source?
[04:45] Jordan Patel: yes it's on github, MIT license; we'll include links.
[04:49] Ethan Brooks: about quota and throttling — we have spikes, need burst capacity. how do you handle spikes?
[04:55] Sofia Ruiz: Dedicated can be configured with burst pools; hosted has adaptive throttling and rate limits, but you can increase quotas for pilots. we also have token-level breakdowns in the console for cost analysis.
[05:07] Lina Zhao: success criteria — let's be explicit. p95 generation < 300ms, schema adherence > 98% on structured outputs, and total token cost less than x (we'll define x after seeing numbers). if we hit these on 48-hour run we consider POC successful.
[05:22] Jordan Patel: noted. we'll propose initial cost targets in the pricing doc. also we'll recommend model variants and quantization profiles to hit cost/latency targets.
[05:31] Marco Silva: what about data residency? some EU users need to stay in eu-west.
[05:35] Jordan Patel: we have region routing; pilot can be run in us-west but production can be pinned to eu regions; for Private deployments you control region.
[05:43] Ethan Brooks: ok next, logistics — deliverables from Redwood for the pilot?
[05:47] Sofia Ruiz: 1) benchmark harness repo + runbook 2) openai-compatible endpoint config 3) sample SDK integration snippets 4) structured-output schema validator 5) cost/throughput recommendation doc.
[05:59] Jordan Patel: we'll also provide a short security pack with SOC2 artifact locations and KMS integration notes.
[06:05] Marco Silva: sounds good. any blockers on our side? we need to prepare traces and whitelist IPs for the bench.
[06:11] Lina Zhao: yes we'll extract 72h trace and top prompt templates. should we anonymize user ids?
[06:16] Sofia Ruiz: anonymize PII but preserve token distribution and session lengths. that is sufficient.
[06:23] Ethan Brooks: timeline recap?
[06:25] Jordan Patel: jordan to send pricing + Dedicated vs Hosted doc by march 1; sofia to upload bench harness by feb 27; halcyon to upload traces by feb 28; schedule 48-hour run week of march 9.
[06:37] Marco Silva: agreed. one quick question — how do you measure schema violations in streaming responses?
[06:43] Sofia Ruiz: we capture the streaming buffer, attempt to parse final JSON and also run an incremental schema validator on the stream. any partial failures are flagged and we sample for manual review.
[06:53] Lina Zhao: okay that helps.
[06:55] Ethan Brooks: any compliance costs associated with Private vs Dedicated?
[06:59] Jordan Patel: Private has setup and operation fees; Dedicated has a premium but lower ops burden. we'll include numbers.
[07:06] Marco Silva: thanks — we'll wait for the docs and get our traces ready.
[07:10] Jordan Patel: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the repo links and calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[07:15] Lina Zhao: thanks all.

End of transcript.
